name: Type II Error
expr: β = P(fail to reject H₀ | H₀ false)

name: Mann-Whitney U Test (concept)
expr: compares ranks of two independent samples

name: p-value (concept)
expr: smallest α at which H₀ is rejected

name: Standard Error of Difference of Means
Trend by Semi-Average Method
expr: trend line joins averages of two halves

name: Kruskal-Wallis Test (concept)
expr: compares ranks across three or more groups

name: Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test (concept)
expr: compares paired samples using signed ranks

name: Runs Test (concept)
expr: tests randomness of a data sequence

name: Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test (concept)
expr: compares sample distribution to a reference distribution

name: Nonresponse Bias (concept)
expr: error from systematic difference in nonrespondents

name: Prior Probability (concept)
expr: initial belief about a parameter before observing data

name: Credible Interval (concept)
expr: interval containing the parameter with a given posterior probability

name: Randomized Block Design (concept)
expr: blocking controls for a known nuisance variable

name: Factorial Design (concept)
expr: tests multiple factors and their interactions simultaneously

name: Latin Square Design (concept)
expr: controls for two nuisance variables using a grid layout

name: Completely Randomized Design (concept)
expr: treatments assigned to units entirely at random

name: Heteroscedasticity (concept)
expr: non-constant variance of residuals across observations

name: Autocorrelation (concept)
expr: correlation of a variable with its own lagged values

name: Life Expectancy (concept)
expr: average years remaining at a given age

name: Net Reproduction Rate (concept)
expr: average number of daughters replacing each woman

name: Principal Component (concept)
expr: linear combination of variables capturing maximum variance

name: Factor Loading (concept)
expr: correlation between an observed variable and an underlying factor

name: Trimmed Mean (concept)
expr: mean after removing a fixed % of extreme values

name: Outlier Boundary (IQR Method)
expr: outlier if x < Q1−1.5·IQR or x > Q3+1.5·IQR

name: Union of Three Mutually Exclusive Events
Weibull Distribution (concept)
expr: used to model reliability and survival/failure times

name: Point-Biserial Correlation (concept)
expr: correlation between a continuous and a binary variable

name: Cook's Distance (concept)
expr: measures the influence of a single data point on a regression fit

name: Leverage (concept)
expr: measures how far a predictor value is from the mean of predictors

name: Critical Value (concept)
expr: threshold value defining the rejection region

name: One-Tailed vs Two-Tailed Test (concept)
expr: set by the direction of the alternative hypothesis

name: McNemar's Test (concept)
expr: tests changes in paired categorical (before/after) data

name: Simple Random Sampling (concept)
expr: every member of the population has an equal chance of selection

name: Convenience Sampling (concept)
expr: a sample chosen based on ease of access

name: Sampling Distribution of the Mean (concept)
expr: distribution of sample means over repeated samples

name: Central Limit Theorem (concept)
expr: sample mean distribution approaches normal as n increases

name: Tukey HSD Test (concept)
expr: post-hoc test comparing all pairs of group means

name: Consumer Price Index (concept)
expr: measures the average price change of a fixed basket of goods

name: Cost of Living Index (concept)
expr: measures the change in cost to maintain a standard of living

name: Spearman's vs Pearson (concept)
expr: used for ordinal or non-linear monotonic relationships

name: Median Test (concept)
expr: compares medians of two or more independent samples

name: Test-Retest Reliability (concept)
expr: correlation between scores from two administrations of the same test

name: Age-Specific Death Rate
expr: ASDR = deaths in age group/mid-year population of age group × 1000

name: CI for Difference of Two Means
Median (Ungrouped, Even n)
expr: average of the two middle values

name: Class Boundaries
expr: Lower boundary = Lower limit - 0.5, Upper boundary = Upper limit + 0.5

name: Tally Marks (concept)
expr: method of recording data in groups of five for frequency tables

name: MANOVA Wilks Lambda (concept)
expr: ratio of within-group to total variance-covariance determinants

name: Kaplan-Meier Estimator (concept)
expr: nonparametric estimate of the survival function from observed lifetimes

name: Bootstrap Estimate (concept)
expr: repeated resampling with replacement to estimate a statistics distribution

name: Jackknife Estimate (concept)
expr: leave-one-out resampling to estimate bias and variance

name: ROC Curve AUC (concept)
expr: area under the true positive vs false positive rate curve

name: Chi-Square Statistic
expr: χ² = Σ(Oᵢ − Eᵢ)²/Eᵢ, O = observed, E = expected

name: Chi-Square Test for Independence (concept)
expr: tests whether two categorical variables are associated using a contingency table

name: Chi-Square Test for Goodness of Fit (concept)
expr: tests whether observed frequencies match an expected theoretical distribution

name: Degrees of Freedom (Chi-Square Goodness of Fit)
expr: df = k − 1, k = number of categories

name: Yates's Continuity Correction
expr: χ² = Σ(|Oᵢ − Eᵢ| − 0.5)²/Eᵢ, used for 2×2 tables

name: Combined Variance of Two Groups
expr: s²_c = [n₁(s₁² + d₁²) + n₂(s₂² + d₂²)]/(n₁+n₂), where dᵢ = x̄ᵢ − x̄_c

name: Addition Rule (Not Mutually Exclusive)
expr: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

name: Odds in Favor of an Event
Incidence Rate
expr: Incidence Rate = New Cases in Period/Population at Risk × Time

name: Prevalence Rate
expr: Prevalence = Total Cases at a Point in Time/Total Population × 100

name: Sensitivity (Medical Test)
expr: Sensitivity = True Positives/(True Positives + False Negatives)

name: Specificity (Medical Test)
expr: Specificity = True Negatives/(True Negatives + False Positives)

name: Positive Predictive Value (PPV)
expr: PPV = True Positives/(True Positives + False Positives)

name: Negative Predictive Value (NPV)
expr: NPV = True Negatives/(True Negatives + False Negatives)

name: Relative Risk (RR)
expr: RR = Incidence in Exposed Group/Incidence in Unexposed Group

name: Case Fatality Rate
expr: CFR = Deaths from Disease/Total Diagnosed Cases × 100

name: Pure Premium
expr: Pure Premium = Total Losses/Number of Exposure Units

name: Loss Ratio
expr: Loss Ratio = Total Claims Paid/Total Premiums Earned × 100

name: Probability of Survival
expr: ₙpₓ = probability a person aged x survives n more years

name: Probability of Death
expr: qₓ = probability a person aged x dies within one year

name: Expected Loss (Insurance)
expr: Expected Loss = Probability of Claim × Claim Amount

name: Combined Ratio (Insurance)
expr: Combined Ratio = Loss Ratio + Expense Ratio

name: Mortality Rate
expr: Mortality Rate = Deaths in Period/Mid-Period Population × 1000

name: p-value (concept)
expr: the probability of observing results as extreme as the sample, assuming the null hypothesis is true

name: Statistical Software (concept)
expr: R, SPSS, Python (pandas/scipy), and Excel are commonly used tools for statistical analysis

name: Random Number Generation (concept)
expr: algorithms that produce sequences of numbers approximating true statistical randomness

name: Simulation (Monte Carlo) (concept)
expr: uses repeated random sampling to estimate the probability of different outcomes

name: Data Visualization — Boxplot (concept)
expr: displays median, quartiles, and outliers of a dataset in one summary chart

name: Data Visualization — Histogram (concept)
expr: shows the frequency distribution of continuous data divided into intervals (bins)

name: Outlier Detection (IQR Method)
expr: a value is an outlier if it is below Q₁ − 1.5×IQR or above Q₃ + 1.5×IQR

name: Z-Score Outlier Detection
expr: a value is typically flagged as an outlier if |z-score| > 3

name: Missing Completely at Random (MCAR) (concept)
expr: the probability of missing data is unrelated to any observed or unobserved values

name: Missing at Random (MAR) (concept)
expr: the probability of missing data depends only on observed data, not the missing values themselves

name: Mean Imputation (concept)
expr: replaces missing values with the mean of the observed values for that variable

name: Listwise Deletion (concept)
expr: removes an entire record from analysis if any of its values are missing

name: Multiple Imputation (concept)
expr: creates several plausible imputed datasets and combines results to account for missing-data uncertainty

name: Winsorization (concept)
expr: limits extreme values by capping them at a specified percentile instead of removing them

name: Meta-Analysis (concept)
expr: statistically combines results from multiple independent studies to estimate an overall effect

name: Fixed-Effects Model (concept)
expr: assumes all studies share one true effect size, differing only by sampling error

name: Random-Effects Model (concept)
expr: assumes true effect sizes vary across studies, adding between-study variance to the estimate

name: Forest Plot (concept)
expr: a graphical display showing effect sizes and confidence intervals from multiple studies

name: Publication Bias (concept)
expr: the tendency for studies with significant/positive results to be published more often than null results

name: Heterogeneity (I² Statistic) (concept)
expr: measures the percentage of variation across studies due to true differences rather than chance

name: Spatial Autocorrelation (concept)
expr: measures how similar nearby locations are with respect to a given variable

name: Moran's I
expr: measures spatial autocorrelation; values range from −1 (dispersed) to +1 (clustered)

name: Kriging (concept)
expr: a geostatistical interpolation method that estimates values at unsampled locations

name: Spatial Weight Matrix (concept)
expr: defines the spatial relationships/neighbors between locations in a dataset

name: Hotspot Analysis (concept)
expr: identifies statistically significant spatial clusters of high or low values

name: Nearest Neighbor Index
expr: NNI = Observed Mean Distance/Expected Mean Distance (for random distribution)

name: Generalized Linear Model (GLM) (concept)
expr: extends linear regression to allow response variables with non-normal error distributions

name: Poisson Regression Model
expr: log(λ) = β₀ + β₁x₁ + ... + βₙxₙ, models count data

name: Link Function (concept)
expr: connects the linear predictor to the mean of the response variable's distribution

name: Deviance (GLM)
expr: measures the goodness of fit of a GLM; lower deviance indicates a better fit

name: Multicollinearity (concept)
expr: occurs when two or more predictor variables are highly correlated, destabilizing regression estimates

name: Variance Inflation Factor (VIF)
expr: VIF = 1/(1 − R²ᵢ), measures multicollinearity for predictor i

name: Panel Data (concept)
expr: data collected on the same subjects/entities across multiple time periods

name: Fixed Effects Model (concept)
expr: controls for unobserved, time-invariant characteristics unique to each entity in panel data

name: Random Effects Model (concept)
expr: assumes entity-specific effects are uncorrelated with the independent variables

name: Within-Group Estimator (concept)
expr: estimates effects using deviations of each variable from its entity-specific mean

name: Hausman Test (concept)
expr: tests whether fixed effects or random effects is the more appropriate panel data model

name: Autocorrelation in Time Series (concept)
expr: measures how correlated a variable is with its own past values

name: Control Chart Upper Control Limit (X-bar Chart)
Control Chart Lower Control Limit (X-bar Chart)
Sigma Level (concept)
expr: measures process capability in terms of standard deviations that fit between the mean and spec limits

name: Contingency Table (concept)
expr: a table displaying the frequency distribution of two or more categorical variables

name: Marginal Frequency
expr: the row or column totals in a contingency table

name: Relative Risk vs Odds Ratio (concept)
expr: relative risk compares probabilities directly; odds ratio compares the odds of an event between groups

name: Cohen's Kappa (Inter-rater Agreement)
expr: κ = (Observed Agreement − Expected Agreement)/(1 − Expected Agreement)

name: Log-Linear Model (concept)
expr: models the expected cell frequencies of a contingency table as a linear function of category effects

name: Ordinal vs Nominal Data (concept)
expr: ordinal data has a meaningful order (e.g. ratings); nominal data has categories with no inherent order

name: Batting Average (Cricket)
expr: Average = Total Runs Scored/Number of Times Out

name: Bowling Average (Cricket)
expr: Average = Total Runs Conceded/Total Wickets Taken

name: Player Efficiency Rating (concept)
expr: a composite statistic summarizing a player's overall per-minute productivity

name: Test Reliability (concept)
expr: the consistency of a test's results across repeated administrations or items

name: Cronbach's Alpha
expr: α = (k/(k−1))(1 − ΣVarianceᵢ/VarianceTotal), k = number of items, measures internal consistency

name: Test Validity (concept)
expr: the degree to which a test accurately measures what it claims to measure

name: Item Difficulty Index
expr: p = Number of Students Answering Correctly/Total Number of Students

name: Item Discrimination Index
expr: D = (Correct in Upper Group − Correct in Lower Group)/Number in Each Group

name: Percentile Rank
expr: Percentile Rank = (Number of Scores Below X/Total Number of Scores) × 100

name: Grade Equivalent Score (concept)
expr: a score expressing a student's performance in terms of a typical grade level

name: Norm-Referenced vs Criterion-Referenced Test (concept)
expr: norm-referenced compares a student to peers; criterion-referenced compares against a fixed standard

name: Air Quality Index (AQI) (concept)
expr: a standardized indicator summarizing pollutant concentration levels for public health reporting

name: Pollution Index
expr: Pollution Index = Measured Concentration/Permissible Standard Limit

name: Environmental Trend Analysis (concept)
expr: statistical methods used to detect long-term changes in environmental variables over time

name: Return Period (Extreme Events)
expr: Return Period = 1/Probability of Exceedance per Year

name: Carbon Footprint Estimation (concept)
expr: the total greenhouse gas emissions caused directly or indirectly by an activity or entity

name: Species Abundance Estimation (concept)
expr: statistical sampling methods used to estimate population sizes of species in an ecosystem

name: Value at Risk (VaR) (concept)
expr: estimates the maximum expected loss of an investment over a given time period at a set confidence level

name: Sharpe Ratio
expr: Sharpe Ratio = (Return − Risk-Free Rate)/Standard Deviation of Return

name: Standard Deviation as Risk Measure (concept)
expr: measures the volatility/dispersion of investment returns around their mean

name: Coefficient of Variation (Risk per Unit Return)
Monte Carlo Simulation in Finance (concept)
expr: uses repeated random sampling to model the probability of different financial outcomes

name: Credit Scoring Model (concept)
expr: a statistical model that estimates the probability a borrower will default on a loan

name: Ogive (Cumulative Frequency Curve) (concept)
expr: a graph plotting cumulative frequency against the upper class boundaries of a distribution

name: Stem-and-Leaf Plot (concept)
expr: displays data by splitting each value into a "stem" (leading digits) and a "leaf" (last digit)

name: Frequency Polygon (concept)
expr: a line graph formed by connecting the midpoints of the tops of a histogram's bars

name: Scatter Plot (concept)
expr: a graph displaying paired data points to visualize the relationship between two variables

name: Pareto Chart (concept)
expr: a bar chart combined with a cumulative line graph, highlighting the most significant factors in a dataset

name: Class Boundaries
expr: Class Boundary = (Upper Limit of one class + Lower Limit of next class)/2

name: Class Width
expr: Class Width = Upper Class Boundary − Lower Class Boundary

name: Kurtosis (concept)
expr: measures the "tailedness" or peakedness of a probability distribution relative to a normal distribution

name: Excess Kurtosis
expr: Excess Kurtosis = Kurtosis − 3 (relative to normal distribution)

name: Leptokurtic vs Platykurtic (concept)
expr: leptokurtic distributions have sharper peaks and fatter tails; platykurtic have flatter peaks and thinner tails

name: Positively vs Negatively Skewed (concept)
expr: positive skew has a longer tail to the right; negative skew has a longer tail to the left

name: Moment Coefficient of Skewness
expr: γ1 = m3/m2^(3/2), m2 and m3 are the 2nd and 3rd central moments

name: Adjusted R²
expr: Adj R² = 1 − [(1 − R²)(n − 1)/(n − k − 1)], k = number of predictors

name: Homoscedasticity (concept)
expr: the assumption that residuals have constant variance across all levels of the independent variable

name: Heteroscedasticity (concept)
expr: occurs when the variance of residuals is not constant, violating a key regression assumption

name: Durbin-Watson Statistic (concept)
expr: tests for autocorrelation in the residuals of a regression analysis

name: Outlier vs Leverage vs Influence Point (concept)
expr: an outlier has an unusual Y value; a leverage point has an unusual X value; an influence point notably changes the regression line

name: Central Limit Theorem (concept)
expr: as sample size increases, the sampling distribution of the mean approaches a normal distribution

name: Sampling Distribution (concept)
expr: the probability distribution of a given statistic based on many random samples from a population

name: Degrees of Freedom (t-distribution)
expr: df = n − 1, for a one-sample t-test

name: Sample Size Determination (Mean)
expr: n = (Z × σ/E)², E = margin of error

name: Mann-Whitney U Test (concept)
expr: a nonparametric test comparing differences between two independent groups using ranked data

name: Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test (concept)
expr: a nonparametric test comparing two related samples or repeated measurements on a single sample

name: Kruskal-Wallis Test (concept)
expr: a nonparametric alternative to one-way ANOVA for comparing three or more independent groups

name: Sign Test (concept)
expr: a simple nonparametric test that uses the sign (positive/negative) of differences between paired observations

name: Runs Test for Randomness (concept)
expr: tests whether a sequence of data occurs in a random order

name: Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test (concept)
expr: compares a sample distribution with a reference distribution, or compares two sample distributions

name: Kendall's Tau (concept)
expr: a nonparametric measure of the ordinal association between two ranked variables

name: Term Frequency (TF)
expr: TF = Number of times a term appears in a document/Total number of terms in that document

name: Inverse Document Frequency (IDF)
expr: IDF = log(Total Documents/Documents Containing the Term)

name: Word Frequency Distribution (concept)
expr: follows Zipf's Law — a word's frequency is inversely proportional to its rank in the frequency table

name: Sentiment Score (concept)
expr: a numeric value representing the positive, negative, or neutral tone of a piece of text

name: Arrival Rate (λ) (concept)
expr: the average number of customers/requests arriving at a system per unit time

name: Service Rate (μ) (concept)
expr: the average number of customers a server can process per unit time

name: Little's Law
expr: L = λW, L = average number in system, W = average time in system

name: Stochastic Process (concept)
expr: a collection of random variables representing the evolution of a system over time

name: Markov Chain (concept)
expr: a stochastic process where the next state depends only on the current state, not the sequence of prior states

name: Transition Probability Matrix (concept)
expr: a matrix giving the probabilities of moving from each state to every other state in one step

name: Stationary Distribution (Markov Chain) (concept)
expr: a probability distribution that remains unchanged as the Markov chain evolves over time

name: Poisson Process (concept)
expr: a stochastic process counting random events occurring independently at a constant average rate

name: Random Walk (concept)
expr: a mathematical path formed by a sequence of random steps, used to model many stochastic phenomena

name: Brownian Motion (Statistical) (concept)
expr: a continuous-time stochastic process modeling random, erratic movement, key in financial modeling

name: Ergodicity (concept)
expr: a property where a process's time average equals its ensemble average over the long run

name: Completely Randomized Design (CRD) (concept)
expr: treatments are assigned to experimental units entirely at random, with no additional grouping

name: Randomized Block Design (RBD) (concept)
expr: experimental units are grouped into blocks of similar units before randomly assigning treatments within each block

name: Latin Square Design (concept)
expr: controls for two blocking factors simultaneously by arranging treatments so each appears once per row and column

name: Factorial Design (concept)
expr: studies the effect of two or more factors simultaneously, including their interactions

name: Main Effect (concept)
expr: the average effect of a factor on the response variable, averaged across levels of other factors

name: Interaction Effect (concept)
expr: occurs when the effect of one factor on the response depends on the level of another factor

name: Replication (concept)
expr: repeating an experiment to increase precision and allow estimation of experimental error

name: Blocking (concept)
expr: grouping similar experimental units together to reduce the effect of known sources of variability

name: Order Statistics (concept)
expr: the values of a sample arranged in ascending order, denoted X(1) ≤ X(2) ≤ ... ≤ X(n)

name: Sample Minimum
expr: X(1) = the smallest value in the ordered sample

name: Sample Maximum
expr: X(n) = the largest value in the ordered sample

name: Rank of a Value
expr: the position of a value when the dataset is sorted in ascending order

name: DMAIC (concept)
expr: Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control — a structured process improvement methodology

name: Defects Per Million Opportunities (DPMO)
expr: DPMO = (Number of Defects/(Number of Units × Opportunities per Unit)) × 1,000,000

name: First Pass Yield (FPY)
expr: FPY = Units Passing Without Rework/Total Units Started

name: Rolled Throughput Yield (RTY)
expr: RTY = Product of the First Pass Yields of Each Process Step

name: Six Sigma Quality Level (concept)
expr: a process achieving Six Sigma has only about 3.4 defects per million opportunities

name: Voice of the Customer (VOC) (concept)
expr: the documented expectations, preferences, and requirements customers have for a product or service

name: Robust Statistic (concept)
expr: a statistical measure that is not overly affected by outliers or small departures from model assumptions

name: Median as a Robust Measure (concept)
expr: the median is less sensitive to outliers than the mean, making it a more robust measure of central tendency

name: Trimmed Mean
expr: the mean calculated after removing a fixed percentage of the smallest and largest values from a dataset

name: Breakdown Point (concept)
expr: the smallest proportion of extreme data points needed to make an estimator arbitrarily inaccurate

name: Winsorized Mean (concept)
expr: a mean calculated after replacing extreme values with the nearest non-extreme values, rather than removing them

name: Huber Loss Function (concept)
expr: a loss function that behaves quadratically for small errors and linearly for large errors, reducing outlier sensitivity

name: A/B Test (concept)
expr: a controlled experiment comparing two variants (A and B) to determine which performs better on a target metric

name: Minimum Detectable Effect (concept)
expr: the smallest true effect size an A/B test is designed to reliably detect

name: Statistical Significance in A/B Testing (concept)
expr: indicates that an observed difference between variants is unlikely to be due to random chance

name: Sample Ratio Mismatch (concept)
expr: occurs when the actual split of traffic between test variants differs unexpectedly from the intended ratio

name: Uplift (A/B Testing)
expr: Uplift = (Metric in Variant B − Metric in Variant A)/Metric in Variant A × 100

name: Multiple Testing Problem (concept)
expr: the increased chance of a false positive when performing many statistical tests simultaneously

name: Bonferroni Correction
expr: adjusted significance level = α/n, n = number of comparisons being made

name: Multi-Armed Bandit (concept)
expr: an adaptive testing approach that dynamically shifts traffic toward better-performing variants during the test
